_doc: Hand corrections applied by the VIEWER to the built tiles (pipeline/overrides.json is the pipeline's own; fold these into the pipeline on the next full rebuild: docs/TODO.md). Local metres (x east, z south). Every entry needs a 'why' and a 'source'. roadSurface: road id -> OSM-style surface (viewer/roadData.js SURFACE). plazas: paved open areas drawn as their own draped mesh (viewer/plazas.js) instead of the grass default; 'courseDeg' = direction of the stone rows (degrees from +x toward +z).

roadSurface._why: Was: the six roads named Place de Saint-Job forced to setts (2026-11-04). Corrected 2026-11-05: the owner checked on site that the ROADS round the Place, tram included, are asphalt with the grooved rails flush in it, as OSM says; the setts are on the SQUARE itself, which stands at sidewalk height with kerbs all round (UrbIS Land cover type P, drawn raised by viewer/surfaces.js with ?roads=surface; the plazas entry below for the default view).

plazas.why: Place de Saint-Job between the setts Chaussée (north) and Avenue du Prince de Ligne: one setts square with rows of plane trees and parking; OSM has no area for it, so it fell back to grass.
plazas.source: outline from the tile's roads.json (road centrelines); surface from the owner's photos 2026-11-04

plazas.why: Place de Saint-Job between Avenue du Prince de Ligne and the Place streets in front of the church (kiosk, terraces): setts.
plazas.source: outline from roads.json; surface from the owner's photos 2026-11-04

flyStart.why: Fly mode starts just above the tip of the Saint-Job church spire (its highest vertex in G4 buildings.bin: 1201.64, 130.25, 549.25), heading over Place de Saint-Job (owner, 2026-11-04).

centreLine._why: Rue Edith Cavell (OSM tertiary -> engine type 'collector') got the type's default dashed centre line; the measured-paint rule removes guessed centre lines on residential types only. The 2024 orthophoto shows no centre line along it (checked at (569, -1300), (540, -1040), (600, -760), (632, -640): parking bays on both sides, a SCHOOL legend, no line), and UrbIS Topo has none. Keys: OSM way ids (every piece rWAY_n of the way).
centreLine._source: UrbIS orthophoto 2024 (CC0), looked at in roads round 5 (2026-11-13)

parkSquares.name: Square des Heros
parkSquares.why: UrbIS maps the whole square (lawns, dolomite paths, the war memorial's terrace) as one street surface of class 'square': the tiles drew it as a raised setts plaza. The park itself (OSM way 23542633) is the hero place's own ground (viewer/heros/); the strip of the surface round it stays, as sidewalk paving.
parkSquares.source: UrbIS StreetSurfaces 40047 minus OSM leisure=park w23542633; Commons / heritage.uccle.be photos (docs/landmarks/HEROS.md)

bridgePlans._doc: OSM way id of a road tagged bridge=yes -> its deck's measured outline (viewer/streets/bridgeDecks.js plan decks; ?bridgeplan=old = the road band). ring: [x, z] outline; free: indices of ring edges that span the cutting (fascia, no wall); walls: the cutting walls under the deck; under: the station floor between them (terrain cut to level).

1342926162._why: The NEW Carsoel deck over Saint-Job station (old 1928 S-curve bridge demolished Jan 2025, new straight deck open to trams 2 June 2025): ~45 m along the railway (29 precast 15 m beams), the road diagonally across it, the tram 92 stop 'Gare de Saint-Job' and bus platforms on it, widened sidewalks with small green beds. The road band of bridgeDecks.js left the platforms, shelters and sidewalks hanging over the cutting (owner playtest 2026-11-16).
1342926162.source: Outline from OSM 2025 (bridge=yes ways 1342926162, 1411905486/88, 1411869726/27/57/58, 1411916284/87/88, stairs 1412205415/17 to the train platforms), the UrbIS orthophoto (construction slab, H6) and the DTM 2021 cutting; L'Avenir 2024-07-15 / Bx1 2025-06 (45 m wide deck, 15 m beams, road diagonal, tram stop on the deck). Axis frame: c = between the two L26 tracks at x 899.6, u along the line.
1342926162._ring: Both ends overlap the UrbIS street polygons by ~1.5 m (the deck top tucks 10 cm under the drawn street there) of Avenue Carsoel exactly (west: tram road be/id/streetsurface/17109 and sidewalks 134927 / 132971, which already have the new layout; east: 28868, 132776, 132777), so the measured street continues the deck without overlap; the north edge at the east end (railed) is the sidewalk's back edge over the opened cutting (the 1928 bridge's site).

buildingLooks._doc: UrbIS solid id -> { style (facades.js wall styles: 0 red brick, 1 brown, 2 yellow, 3 white render, 4 cream, 5 grey), roofColor (linear rgb; red-orange = clay tiles), bayScale [s, nx, nz] (the face facing (nx, nz) lays its painted window grid out in u x s: a narrow front with more windows than the 2.6 m bays give; facadeGeom.js) }: the looks a local recognises, each checked on Street View (look only). ?looks=old: none. type (viewer/buildingTypes.js TYPE: 0 generic, 1 maison de maitre, 2 art deco / modernist, 3 bel-etage, 4 block, 5 villa), garage false (no garage door).

infillBuildings._doc: Houses UrbIS 3D has no geometry for (null shapes in the BuildingSolids SHP: 631 of 41,231 solids on the Uccle sheets), rebuilt as a gable solid from measured data by tools/infill/infill_buildings.py (appended to data/tiles/<T>/buildings.json + .bin; CHM 'trees' under the roof dropped). streetSurfaces._doc: UrbIS street surface id -> { surface (OSM-style, viewer/roadData.js SURFACE), why, source }: the carriageway surface of single measured surfaces (and `roads`: the OSM roads.json ids whose engine carriageway is kept over them, viewer/surfaces.js engineSurf), where the name vote of viewer/surfaces.js cannot see it (UrbIS names are French only, OSM's are bilingual: they never match). Applied in the tile worker (viewer/tileData.js); ?cortenbosch=old: none.

gardenRestyle._doc: Polygons (city x, z) where the generated front-garden pieces (viewer/gardens/cityGardens.js: brick walls, railings, pillars, driveway gates) are what a local would NOT see: inside, every wall / railing run becomes a clipped hedge of `hedge` (gardenHedge.js species) `height` m high, set back off the street, the pillars and gates go (the driveways stay open). ?cortenbosch=old: none.

cortenbosch_lane.why: Chemin privé 't Cortenbosch's 1990s part: every plot is closed by a clipped beech hedge (copper-brown leaves held all winter; a few ivy hedges), open driveways, no walls, no brick pillars, no iron gates (the kit drew red-brick walls, pillars and black gates)
